draft.briefing: Hey, you're on Swaraj Round in Thrissur! The whole city circles the Vadakkunnathan Temple in the middle. Once a year, Thrissur Pooram fills this ground with elephants and fireworks.
draft.hungryLine: Thrissur loves its vegetarian meals and its strong filter coffee. Here's where to find both.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk around Vadakkunnathan Temple, then visit the cathedral and the tall Puthanpally church tower.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit in the shade of Thekkinkadu Maidan, the big ground around the temple.
moodReplies.surprise-me: During Pooram, two temples face off with dozens of decorated elephants and a contest of colourful umbrellas.

spots.name: Vadakkunnathan Temple
spots.detail: In the middle · Hindus only inside

spots.name: Puthanpally Church
spots.detail: 10 min walk · A very tall tower

legends.title: A festival from a king
legends.body: Raja Sakthan Thampuran started Thrissur Pooram in the late 1700s. It's still the biggest temple festival in Kerala.

legends.title: A temple of wood and murals
legends.body: The temple's old wood carvings and murals won a UNESCO award for conservation.

tips.title: Walk the Round in the evening.
tips.body: It's cooler, and the shops light up.

tips.title: Pooram crowds are huge.
tips.body: Book a stay early if you're here in April or May.

story.title: A temple on a hill
story.body: Vadakkunnathan Temple sits on a small hill. Legend says Parashurama founded it.

story.title: The king who built the city
story.body: Raja Rama Varma, known as Sakthan Thampuran, cleared the forest around the temple and laid out the Round.

story.title: Pooram begins
story.body: He brought neighbouring temples together for one great festival: Thrissur Pooram.

story.title: A city of churches and commerce
story.body: Christian traders and churches grew alongside the temple, and Thrissur became a busy market town.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Walk the Round, see the temple, climb the church tower. Tell me which view you liked.
